en gran.explanation: "En gran" means "a spruce / fir". To name one kind of fir, use "en nordmannsgran" (a Nordmann fir): "Vi har en nordmannsgran i stuen" (We have a Nordmann fir in the living room).

en granat.explanation: "En granat" means "a grenade". Do not mix it up with "et granatæble" (a pomegranate), which is built from "granat" and "et æble" (an apple): "Jeg spiser et granatæble" (I eat a pomegranate).

en gratisavis.explanation: "En gratisavis" means "a free newspaper". It is built from "gratis" (free) and "en avis" (a newspaper).

en grav.explanation: "En grav" means "a grave". The same word also names a long ditch dug in the ground, as in "en voldgrav" (a moat).

en graviditet.explanation: "En graviditet" means "a pregnancy". It is built from "gravid" (pregnant). To say a woman is pregnant, say: "Hun er gravid" (She is pregnant).

en graviditetstest.explanation: "En graviditetstest" means "a pregnancy test". It is built from "graviditet" (pregnancy) and "en test" (a test). To say you do one, use "tage" (take): "Jeg tager en graviditetstest" (I take a pregnancy test).

en gravko.explanation: "En gravko" means "an excavator". It is built on the verb "at grave" (to dig).

en gravsten.explanation: "En gravsten" means "a gravestone". It is built from "en grav" (a grave) and "en sten" (a stone). To say you lay flowers there, say: "Jeg lægger blomster ved gravstenen" (I lay flowers at the gravestone).

en gren.explanation: "En gren" means "a branch", as in a tree. To talk about a small thin branch, use "en kvist" (a twig): "Der ligger en kvist på stien" (There is a twig on the path).

en grill.explanation: "En grill" means "a grill". The matching verb is "at grille" (to grill). To say what you grill, put the food after the verb: "Vi griller pølser" (We grill sausages).

en grillbar.explanation: "En grillbar" means "a grill bar". It is built from "en grill" (a grill) and "en bar" (a bar).

en grillfest.explanation: "En grillfest" means "a barbecue party". It is built from "en grill" (a grill) and "en fest" (a party). To say you are barbecuing, use the verb "at grille" (to grill): "Vi griller i aften" (We are barbecuing tonight).

en grimasse.explanation: "En grimasse" means "a grimace". To say someone pulls faces, use "at skære grimasser" (to pull faces), where "skære" otherwise means "to cut": "Børnene skærer grimasser" (The children are pulling faces).

en gris.explanation: "En gris" means "a pig". Said about a person, it is rude: "Du er en gris!" (You are a pig!)

en grund.explanation: "En grund" means "a reason". To say "for that reason", use "af den grund": "Han var syg, og af den grund blev han hjemme" (He was ill, and for that reason he stayed home). To say a plot of land, the same word is used: "Vi køber en grund og bygger et hus" (We buy a plot of land and build a house).

en grundlov.explanation: "En grundlov" means "a constitution". It is built from "grund" (base) and "en lov" (a law). In Denmark, 5 June is "Grundlovsdag" (Constitution Day).

en grundskole.explanation: "En grundskole" means "a primary school". In Denmark it covers ten years, from 0th grade to 9th grade, not just the first years.

en gruppe.explanation: "En gruppe" means "a group". To say what the group is made of, put the word right after "gruppe", with no word for "of": "en gruppe børn" (a group of children).

en gryde.explanation: "En gryde" means "a pot". To say what is in the pot, put the food right after "gryde": "Vi laver en gryde suppe" (We make a pot of soup). To talk about the pan for frying, use "en pande" (a pan): "Jeg steger æg på en pande" (I fry eggs in a pan).

en grydelap.explanation: "En grydelap" means "a pot holder". It is built from "en gryde" (a pot) and "en lap" (a piece of cloth).

en grænse.explanation: "En grænse" means "a border". Denmark's only land border is the one with Germany: "grænsen til Tyskland" (the border with Germany). To talk about a limit, the same word is used: "Alt har en grænse" (Everything has a limit).

en grænseværdi.explanation: "En grænseværdi" means "a limit value". It is built from "grænse" (limit) and "en værdi" (a value). To say the limit is passed, use "overskride" (exceed): "Vandet overskrider grænseværdien" (The water exceeds the limit value).

en græshoppe.explanation: "En græshoppe" means "a grasshopper". The first part of the word is "græs" (grass).

en græsslåmaskine.explanation: "En græsslåmaskine" means "a lawnmower". It is built from "græs" (grass), "at slå" (to mow) and "en maskine" (a machine). The verb "slå" normally means "to hit", so "at slå græs" is literally "to hit grass": "Jeg slår græsset" (I mow the grass).

en græsslåning.explanation: "En græsslåning" means "a lawn mowing". It is built from "græs" (grass) and the verb "at slå" (to mow). The verb "slå" normally means "to hit": "Jeg slår græs i dag" (I mow the grass today).
